A smooth real background theta is nef if theta+epsilon h has a strictly positive smooth dd^c-potential representative for every epsilon>0, where h is a fixed Hermitian metric; it is big if theta+dd^c u>=delta h for some delta>0 and genuine global quasi-psh u. Neither property assumes d-closedness. For every smooth positive Gauduchon metric gamma with dd^c gamma^(n-1)=0 define D_mu(gamma)=integral (mu/gamma^n)^(1/n) gamma^n, lambda_mu(theta)=inf_gamma integral theta wedge gamma^(n-1)/D_mu(gamma), and V_mu(theta)=lambda_mu(theta)^n for nef theta, using decreasing epsilon-regularization at a nef boundary. Every Gauduchon metric participates. Let theta_s=theta-s eta have strictly positive smooth dd^c-potential representatives for 0<=s<t, with a nef endpoint theta_t. If gamma_s is a minimizing Gauduchon metric for the fixed-density quotient, the first-variation identity on positive compact path segments is d/ds lambda_mu(theta_s)=-integral eta wedge gamma_s^(n-1)/D_mu(gamma_s). The proposed endpoint identity lambda_mu(theta_t)=lambda_mu(theta)-integral_0^t integral eta wedge gamma_s^(n-1)/D_mu(gamma_s) ds requires an actual endpoint limit and justified improper integral. Original P14 asks for geometric hypotheses controlling this cost up to the nef endpoint beyond a closed nef positive-volume core plus semipositive summand, and asks when positive root volume forces bigness without that core. Compare closed-background conclusions with the classical Kähler nef Morse bound vol(alpha-beta)>=integral alpha^n-n integral alpha^(n-1) beta in its exact valid setting. For genuinely nonclosed backgrounds retain differential/torsion information and dependence on mu; ordinary intersection numbers need not be invariant under smooth dd^c gauge. ## C. Quantitative geometric cost profiles

Suppose {a=0} is a smooth compact real submanifold of codimension d>0,
with two-sided a comparable to distance^k,k>0, in a fixed tube and

 r<1: C(t-epsilon) comparable to epsilon^((1-r)/n-1);
